# GLP-1, weight-loss and diabetes medicines — explained clearly

Approvals, label dosing, side effects, costs and the legal ways to get every GLP-1, incretin and insulin medicine in the United States and Canada.

⌘K

**medicines**: 26

**comparisons**: 6

**answered questions**: 28

**buying & safety guides**: 6

What is a GLP-1?
A **GLP-1 receptor agonist** is a medicine that mimics the gut hormone GLP-1: it raises insulin after meals, lowers glucagon, slows stomach emptying and reduces appetite. Semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy) and tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound) are the best known; all are prescription-only in the US and Canada. [Read the full answer ](https://www.glpatlas.com/questions/what-is-glp1/)

Title: Ozempic (semaglutide): Uses, Dosage, Side Effects & Cost
Summary: Ozempic (semaglutide) by Novo Nordisk: what it treats, label dosing, side effects, cost and legal ways to get it in the US and Canada.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

GLP-1 & incretin medicines
# Ozempic (injection)

semaglutide · GLP-1 receptor agonist · Novo Nordisk
✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

In short
**Ozempic** (semaglutide) is a GLP-1 receptor agonist made by Novo Nordisk, used for blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes, lower risk of major cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes and heart disease and reduce risk of kidney disease progression in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease. Schedule: once weekly. It is prescription-only in the US and Canada.

**Form**Prefilled pen, subcutaneous injection
**How often**Once weekly

**United States**FDA-approved (type 2 diabetes). Not approved for weight loss — Wegovy is the semaglutide brand for that.
**Canada**Approved in Canada. Health Canada has also authorized generic semaglutide injections for type 2 diabetes (Dr. Reddy's, April 28, 2026; Apotex, May 1, 2026).
**Prescription**Required
**⚠ Boxed warning: risk of thyroid C-cell tumors. Do not use if you or a family member has had medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or if you have Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).**

## What it is used for

- Blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes
- Lower risk of major cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes and heart disease
- Reduce risk of kidney disease progression in adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease

## Ozempic dosage

Per the official label. Your prescriber sets your dose — never change it on your own.

| 1Weeks 1–4 | 0.25 mg once weekly (starter dose) |
| 2Weeks 5–8 | 0.5 mg once weekly |
| 3If more control is needed | 1 mg, then 2 mg once weekly, each after at least 4 weeks |
| 4Maximum | 2 mg once weekly |

### How to take it

Inject under the skin of the stomach, thigh or upper arm on the same day each week, with or without food. Rotate injection sites.
### Storage

Before first use: refrigerate 36–46°F (2–8°C). After first use: room temperature or fridge for up to 56 days. Do not freeze.

## Side effects

### Common

- Nausea
- Diarrhea
- Vomiting
- Constipation
- Abdominal pain
- Indigestion / heartburn
- Fatigue
- Decreased appetite

### Serious — get medical help

- Pancreatitis (severe stomach pain that may spread to the back)
- Gallbladder problems, including gallstones
- Low blood sugar when combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea
- Kidney problems, often from dehydration after vomiting or diarrhea
- Serious allergic reactions
- Diabetic retinopathy complications (people with type 2 diabetes)
- Pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation — tell your surgical team you take it
### Who should not use it

- Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, or MEN 2
- Prior serious allergic reaction to the drug or its ingredients
- Pregnancy (stop before a planned pregnancy as advised by your prescriber)
- Use together with another GLP-1 receptor agonist

## Cost

US self-pay through NovoCare and partner pharmacies has been about $349/month for most doses (higher for 2 mg). With commercial insurance, savings cards can lower copays. Verify current prices before you fill.
[GLP-1 cost without insurance ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/glp1-cost-without-insurance/)

## How to buy Ozempic legally

- Get a prescription from your doctor or a licensed telehealth provider.

- Fill it at a licensed pharmacy, or through the manufacturer's self-pay pharmacy.

- Verify any online pharmacy first (US: [safe.pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/); Canada: your provincial pharmacy college register).

[Buying legally in the USA ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-usa/) [Buying legally in Canada ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-canada/)

## Frequently asked questions

Is Ozempic approved for weight loss?

No. Ozempic is approved for type 2 diabetes. The same molecule at weight-management doses is sold as Wegovy.Is there a generic Ozempic?

In Canada, yes: Health Canada authorized generic semaglutide injections in April and May 2026. In the US there is no FDA-approved generic as of October 2026.Is compounded semaglutide the same as Ozempic?

No. Compounded or 'research' semaglutide is not FDA-approved, and the FDA has warned about dosing errors and unknown ingredients.

Title: Ozempic tablets: Uses, Dosage, Side Effects & Cost

GLP-1 & incretin medicines
# Ozempic tablets (formerly Rybelsus)

oral semaglutide · GLP-1 receptor agonist (oral) · Novo Nordisk
✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

In short
**Ozempic tablets** (oral semaglutide) is a GLP-1 receptor agonist (oral) made by Novo Nordisk, used for blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes and lower risk of major cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes at high risk. Schedule: once daily. It is prescription-only in the US and Canada.

**Form**Tablet
**How often**Once daily

**United States**FDA approved the Ozempic name for oral semaglutide 1.5 mg, 4 mg and 9 mg tablets on February 4, 2026; US launch May 4, 2026. Rybelsus 3/7/14 mg remains available during the transition. A 25 mg tablet is under FDA review.
**Canada**Rybelsus is approved in Canada; check the Health Canada Drug Product Database for the current brand name.
**Prescription**Required
**⚠ Boxed warning: risk of thyroid C-cell tumors. Do not use if you or a family member has had medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or if you have Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).**

## What it is used for

- Blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes
- Lower risk of major cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes at high risk

## Ozempic tablets dosage

Per the official label. Your prescriber sets your dose — never change it on your own.

| 1Days 1–30 | 1.5 mg once daily (Rybelsus: 3 mg) |
| 2Day 31 on | 4 mg once daily (Rybelsus: 7 mg) |
| 3If more control is needed | 9 mg once daily after at least 30 days (Rybelsus: 14 mg) |

### How to take it

Take first thing in the morning on an empty stomach with no more than 4 oz (120 mL) of plain water. Wait at least 30 minutes before eating, drinking or taking other oral medicines. Swallow whole.
### Storage

Keep in the original bottle, away from light and moisture.

## Side effects

### Common

- Nausea
- Diarrhea
- Vomiting
- Constipation
- Abdominal pain
- Indigestion / heartburn
- Fatigue
- Decreased appetite

### Serious — get medical help

- Pancreatitis (severe stomach pain that may spread to the back)
- Gallbladder problems, including gallstones
- Low blood sugar when combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea
- Kidney problems, often from dehydration after vomiting or diarrhea
- Serious allergic reactions
- Diabetic retinopathy complications (people with type 2 diabetes)
- Pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation — tell your surgical team you take it
### Who should not use it

- Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, or MEN 2
- Prior serious allergic reaction to the drug or its ingredients
- Pregnancy (stop before a planned pregnancy as advised by your prescriber)
- Use together with another GLP-1 receptor agonist

## Cost

Brand-only in the US. Check NovoCare and manufacturer savings programs.
[GLP-1 cost without insurance ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/glp1-cost-without-insurance/)

## How to buy Ozempic tablets legally

- Get a prescription from your doctor or a licensed telehealth provider.

- Fill it at a licensed pharmacy, or through the manufacturer's self-pay pharmacy.

- Verify any online pharmacy first (US: [safe.pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/); Canada: your provincial pharmacy college register).

[Buying legally in the USA ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-usa/) [Buying legally in Canada ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-canada/)

## Frequently asked questions

Can I swap Rybelsus and Ozempic tablets mg for mg?

No. The new tablets absorb better, so doses differ: Rybelsus 7 mg corresponds to Ozempic 4 mg, and 14 mg to 9 mg. Your prescriber handles the switch.Why the name change?

Novo Nordisk moved oral semaglutide for diabetes under the better-known Ozempic name in 2026.
**Also searched as:** Ozempic pill, Ozempic tablet, oral Ozempic, Rybelsus, Rybelsus 3 mg, Rybelsus 7 mg, Rybelsus 14 mg, oral semaglutide, semaglutide tablets, semaglutide pill, Rybelsis, Rybelus

Title: Wegovy (semaglutide): Uses, Dosage, Side Effects & Cost
Summary: Wegovy (semaglutide) by Novo Nordisk: what it treats, label dosing, side effects, cost and legal ways to get it in the US and Canada.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

GLP-1 & incretin medicines
# Wegovy (injection)

semaglutide · GLP-1 receptor agonist · Novo Nordisk
✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

In short
**Wegovy** (semaglutide) is a GLP-1 receptor agonist made by Novo Nordisk, used for weight reduction and long-term maintenance in adults and children 12+ with obesity, or adults with overweight and a weight-related condition, reduce major cardiovascular events in adults with heart disease and obesity or overweight and MASH (fatty liver disease) with moderate-to-advanced fibrosis in adults. Schedule: once weekly. It is prescription-only in the US and Canada.

**Form**Single-dose prefilled pen, subcutaneous injection
**How often**Once weekly

**United States**FDA-approved. A higher 7.2 mg dose, Wegovy HD, was approved March 19, 2026.
**Canada**Approved in Canada. Health Canada authorized the first generic semaglutide for weight management on June 29, 2026.
**Prescription**Required
**⚠ Boxed warning: risk of thyroid C-cell tumors. Do not use if you or a family member has had medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or if you have Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).**

## What it is used for

- Weight reduction and long-term maintenance in adults and children 12+ with obesity, or adults with overweight and a weight-related condition
- Reduce major cardiovascular events in adults with heart disease and obesity or overweight
- MASH (fatty liver disease) with moderate-to-advanced fibrosis in adults

## Wegovy dosage

Per the official label. Your prescriber sets your dose — never change it on your own.

| 1Weeks 1–4 | 0.25 mg weekly |
| 2Weeks 5–8 | 0.5 mg weekly |
| 3Weeks 9–12 | 1 mg weekly |
| 4Weeks 13–16 | 1.7 mg weekly |
| 5Week 17 on | 2.4 mg weekly (or 1.7 mg if 2.4 mg is not tolerated) |
| 6Wegovy HD | 7.2 mg weekly for adults who have tolerated 2.4 mg for at least 4 weeks |

### How to take it

Inject under the skin of the stomach, thigh or upper arm on the same day each week.
### Storage

Refrigerate 36–46°F (2–8°C). May be kept at up to 86°F (30°C) for up to 28 days. Do not freeze.

## Side effects

### Common

- Nausea
- Diarrhea
- Vomiting
- Constipation
- Abdominal pain
- Indigestion / heartburn
- Fatigue
- Decreased appetite

### Serious — get medical help

- Pancreatitis (severe stomach pain that may spread to the back)
- Gallbladder problems, including gallstones
- Low blood sugar when combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea
- Kidney problems, often from dehydration after vomiting or diarrhea
- Serious allergic reactions
- Diabetic retinopathy complications (people with type 2 diabetes)
- Pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation — tell your surgical team you take it
### Who should not use it

- Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, or MEN 2
- Prior serious allergic reaction to the drug or its ingredients
- Pregnancy (stop before a planned pregnancy as advised by your prescriber)
- Use together with another GLP-1 receptor agonist

## Cost

US self-pay through NovoCare and partners has been about $349/month for 0.25–2.4 mg, with intro offers on starter doses; Wegovy HD self-pay was listed around $399/month. Verify before filling.
[GLP-1 cost without insurance ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/glp1-cost-without-insurance/)

- Get a prescription from your doctor or a licensed telehealth provider.

- Fill it at a licensed pharmacy, or through the manufacturer's self-pay pharmacy.

- Verify any online pharmacy first (US: [safe.pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/); Canada: your provincial pharmacy college register).

## Frequently asked questions

Wegovy vs Ozempic: what's the difference?

Same molecule, different approvals and doses. Wegovy is for weight management (up to 2.4 mg, or 7.2 mg as Wegovy HD); Ozempic is for type 2 diabetes (up to 2 mg).What is Wegovy HD?

A 7.2 mg weekly dose approved in March 2026. In the STEP UP trial it produced about 21% average weight loss versus about 18% for 2.4 mg. Altered skin sensation was more common at the higher dose.Do I have to stay on Wegovy?

Studies show weight often returns after stopping. Long-term plans should be agreed with your prescriber.

| 1Days 1–30 | 1.5 mg daily |
| 2Days 31–60 | 4 mg daily |
| 3Days 61–90 | 9 mg daily |
| 4Day 91 on | 25 mg daily (maintenance) |

Take on an empty stomach with up to 4 oz of water. Wait at least 30 minutes before food, drink or other oral medicines. Swallow whole.

| 4Maximum | 15 mg weekly |

### How to take it

Inject under the skin of the stomach, thigh or upper arm once weekly, any time of day, with or without food.
### Storage

- Kidney problems, often from dehydration after vomiting or diarrhea
- Serious allergic reactions
- Diabetic retinopathy complications (people with type 2 diabetes)
- Pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation — tell your surgical team you take it

# Foundayo

orforglipron · Small-molecule (non-peptide) oral GLP-1 receptor agonist · Eli Lilly
✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

In short
**Foundayo** (orforglipron) is a small-molecule (non-peptide) oral GLP-1 receptor agonist made by Eli Lilly, used for weight reduction and long-term maintenance in adults with obesity, or overweight with at least one weight-related condition. Schedule: once daily. It is prescription-only in the US and Canada.

**Form**Tablet
**How often**Once daily

**United States**FDA-approved April 1, 2026. Not approved for type 2 diabetes in the US (Lilly has filed in many countries).
**Canada**Check the Health Canada Drug Product Database for current status.
**Prescription**Required
**⚠ Boxed warning: risk of thyroid C-cell tumors. Do not use if you or a family member has had medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or if you have Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).**

## What it is used for

- Weight reduction and long-term maintenance in adults with obesity, or overweight with at least one weight-related condition

## Foundayo dosage

Per the official label. Your prescriber sets your dose — never change it on your own.

| 1Days 1–30 | 0.8 mg daily |
| 2Days 31–60 | 2.5 mg daily |
| 3Days 61–90 | 5.5 mg daily (lowest maintenance dose) |
| 4If needed | 9 mg, 14.5 mg or 17.2 mg daily, each step after at least 30 days |
| 5Maximum | 17.2 mg daily (9 mg with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors) |

### How to take it

Take once daily at any time, with or without food or water — no fasting rule.
### Storage

Room temperature in the original container.

## Side effects

### Common

- Nausea
- Diarrhea
- Vomiting
- Constipation
- Abdominal pain
- Indigestion / heartburn
- Fatigue
- Decreased appetite

### Serious — get medical help

- Pancreatitis (severe stomach pain that may spread to the back)
- Gallbladder problems, including gallstones
- Low blood sugar when combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea
- Kidney problems, often from dehydration after vomiting or diarrhea
- Serious allergic reactions
- Diabetic retinopathy complications (people with type 2 diabetes)
- Pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation — tell your surgical team you take it
### Who should not use it

- Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, or MEN 2
- Prior serious allergic reaction to the drug or its ingredients
- Pregnancy (stop before a planned pregnancy as advised by your prescriber)
- Use together with another GLP-1 receptor agonist

## Cost

LillyDirect self-pay launched at $149/month (0.8 mg), $199 (2.5 mg) and $299 (higher doses). With commercial coverage, a savings card may bring it to $25/month. Verify before filling.
[GLP-1 cost without insurance ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/glp1-cost-without-insurance/)

## How to buy Foundayo legally

- Get a prescription from your doctor or a licensed telehealth provider.

- Fill it at a licensed pharmacy, or through the manufacturer's self-pay pharmacy.

- Verify any online pharmacy first (US: [safe.pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/); Canada: your provincial pharmacy college register).

[Buying legally in the USA ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-usa/) [Buying legally in Canada ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-canada/)

## Common questions

- [Does Wegovy or Zepbound cause hair loss?](https://www.glpatlas.com/questions/glp1-hair-loss/)
- [What is a GLP-1 agonist?](https://www.glpatlas.com/questions/what-is-glp1/)
- [Who qualifies for Wegovy or Zepbound?](https://www.glpatlas.com/questions/glp1-who-qualifies/)

## Frequently asked questions

How is Foundayo different from the Wegovy pill?

Foundayo is a small molecule with no food or water restrictions. The Wegovy pill is semaglutide and must be taken fasting.How much weight do people lose on Foundayo?

In the 72-week ATTAIN-1 trial, the highest dose averaged about 12% body-weight loss versus about 1% on placebo.
**Also searched as:** orforglipron, Foundayo pill, Foundayo tablet, Lilly weight loss pill, Foundayo price, Foundayo side effects, orforglipron price, Fondayo, Foundyo

GLP-1 & incretin medicines
# Victoza (and generic liraglutide)

liraglutide · GLP-1 receptor agonist · Novo Nordisk; generics available
✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

In short
**Victoza** (liraglutide) is a GLP-1 receptor agonist made by Novo Nordisk; generics available, used for blood sugar control in adults and children 10+ with type 2 diabetes and lower cardiovascular risk in adults with type 2 diabetes and heart disease. Schedule: once daily. It is prescription-only in the US and Canada.

**Form**Prefilled multi-dose pen
**How often**Once daily

**United States**FDA-approved; generic liraglutide (Victoza equivalent) is available.
**Canada**Approved in Canada.
**Prescription**Required
**⚠ Boxed warning: risk of thyroid C-cell tumors. Do not use if you or a family member has had medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or if you have Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).**

## What it is used for

- Blood sugar control in adults and children 10+ with type 2 diabetes
- Lower cardiovascular risk in adults with type 2 diabetes and heart disease

## Victoza dosage

Per the official label. Your prescriber sets your dose — never change it on your own.

| 1Week 1 | 0.6 mg daily (starter) |
| 2Week 2 on | 1.2 mg daily |
| 3If needed | 1.8 mg daily |

### How to take it

Inject once daily at any time, independent of meals.
### Storage

Refrigerate before first use; after first use up to 30 days at room temperature or in the fridge.

## Side effects

### Common

- Nausea
- Diarrhea
- Vomiting
- Constipation
- Abdominal pain
- Indigestion / heartburn
- Fatigue
- Decreased appetite

### Serious — get medical help

- Pancreatitis (severe stomach pain that may spread to the back)
- Gallbladder problems, including gallstones
- Low blood sugar when combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea
- Kidney problems, often from dehydration after vomiting or diarrhea
- Serious allergic reactions
- Diabetic retinopathy complications (people with type 2 diabetes)
- Pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation — tell your surgical team you take it
### Who should not use it

- Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, or MEN 2
- Prior serious allergic reaction to the drug or its ingredients
- Pregnancy (stop before a planned pregnancy as advised by your prescriber)
- Use together with another GLP-1 receptor agonist

## Cost

Generic liraglutide is typically far cheaper than branded weekly GLP-1s. Check discount programs.
[GLP-1 cost without insurance ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/glp1-cost-without-insurance/)

## How to buy Victoza legally

- Get a prescription from your doctor or a licensed telehealth provider.

- Fill it at a licensed pharmacy, or through the manufacturer's self-pay pharmacy.

- Verify any online pharmacy first (US: [safe.pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/); Canada: your provincial pharmacy college register).

[Buying legally in the USA ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-usa/) [Buying legally in Canada ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-canada/)

## Frequently asked questions

Is Victoza the same as Saxenda?

Same molecule. Saxenda uses higher doses (up to 3 mg) for weight management.
**Also searched as:** liraglutide, generic liraglutide, Victoza pen, Victosa, liraglutide injection

# Trulicity

dulaglutide · GLP-1 receptor agonist · Eli Lilly
✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

In short
**Trulicity** (dulaglutide) is a GLP-1 receptor agonist made by Eli Lilly, used for blood sugar control in adults and children 10+ with type 2 diabetes and lower cardiovascular risk in adults with type 2 diabetes. Schedule: once weekly. It is prescription-only in the US and Canada.

**Form**Single-dose pen
**How often**Once weekly

**United States**FDA-approved.
**Canada**Approved in Canada.
**Prescription**Required
**⚠ Boxed warning: risk of thyroid C-cell tumors. Do not use if you or a family member has had medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or if you have Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).**

## What it is used for

- Blood sugar control in adults and children 10+ with type 2 diabetes
- Lower cardiovascular risk in adults with type 2 diabetes

## Trulicity dosage

Per the official label. Your prescriber sets your dose — never change it on your own.

| 1Start | 0.75 mg weekly |
| 2If needed | 1.5 mg, then 3 mg, then 4.5 mg weekly, each after at least 4 weeks |
| 3Maximum | 4.5 mg weekly |

### How to take it

Inject once weekly, any time of day, with or without food.
### Storage

Refrigerate; may be kept at room temperature up to 14 days.

## Side effects

### Common

- Nausea
- Diarrhea
- Vomiting
- Constipation
- Abdominal pain
- Indigestion / heartburn
- Fatigue
- Decreased appetite

### Serious — get medical help

- Pancreatitis (severe stomach pain that may spread to the back)
- Gallbladder problems, including gallstones
- Low blood sugar when combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea
- Kidney problems, often from dehydration after vomiting or diarrhea
- Serious allergic reactions
- Diabetic retinopathy complications (people with type 2 diabetes)
- Pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation — tell your surgical team you take it
### Who should not use it

- Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, or MEN 2
- Prior serious allergic reaction to the drug or its ingredients
- Pregnancy (stop before a planned pregnancy as advised by your prescriber)
- Use together with another GLP-1 receptor agonist

## Cost

Lilly has offered Trulicity through LillyDirect at discounts off list price. Verify current pricing.
[GLP-1 cost without insurance ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/glp1-cost-without-insurance/)

## How to buy Trulicity legally

- Get a prescription from your doctor or a licensed telehealth provider.

- Fill it at a licensed pharmacy, or through the manufacturer's self-pay pharmacy.

- Verify any online pharmacy first (US: [safe.pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/); Canada: your provincial pharmacy college register).

[Buying legally in the USA ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-usa/) [Buying legally in Canada ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-canada/)

Is Trulicity used for weight loss?

It is approved for type 2 diabetes. Some weight loss can occur, but it is not approved as a weight-management drug.

# Byetta and Bydureon BCise

exenatide · GLP-1 receptor agonist · AstraZeneca
✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

In short
**Exenatide** (exenatide) is a GLP-1 receptor agonist made by AstraZeneca, used for blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes. Schedule: twice daily (byetta) or once weekly (bydureon bcise). It is prescription-only in the US and Canada.

**Form**Pen injection
**How often**Twice daily (Byetta) or once weekly (Bydureon BCise)

**United States**Largely withdrawn from the US market; availability is limited. Ask a pharmacist before relying on supply.
**Canada**Check the Drug Product Database for current marketing status.
**Prescription**Required
**⚠ Bydureon BCise carries the thyroid C-cell tumor boxed warning; twice-daily Byetta does not.**

## What it is used for

- Blood sugar control in type 2 diabetes

## Exenatide dosage

Per the official label. Your prescriber sets your dose — never change it on your own.

| 1Byetta | 5 mcg twice daily within 60 minutes before morning and evening meals; may increase to 10 mcg after 1 month |
| 2Bydureon BCise | 2 mg once weekly |

### How to take it

Byetta: before meals. Bydureon BCise: same day each week, with or without meals.
### Storage

Refrigerate.

## Side effects

### Common

- Nausea
- Diarrhea
- Vomiting
- Constipation
- Abdominal pain
- Indigestion / heartburn
- Fatigue
- Decreased appetite

### Serious — get medical help

- Pancreatitis (severe stomach pain that may spread to the back)
- Gallbladder problems, including gallstones
- Low blood sugar when combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea
- Kidney problems, often from dehydration after vomiting or diarrhea
- Serious allergic reactions
- Diabetic retinopathy complications (people with type 2 diabetes)
- Pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation — tell your surgical team you take it
### Who should not use it

- Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, or MEN 2
- Prior serious allergic reaction to the drug or its ingredients
- Pregnancy (stop before a planned pregnancy as advised by your prescriber)
- Use together with another GLP-1 receptor agonist

## Cost

Limited availability; prices vary.
[GLP-1 cost without insurance ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/glp1-cost-without-insurance/)

## How to buy Exenatide legally

- Get a prescription from your doctor or a licensed telehealth provider.

- Fill it at a licensed pharmacy.

- Verify any online pharmacy first (US: [safe.pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/); Canada: your provincial pharmacy college register).

[Buying legally in the USA ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-usa/) [Buying legally in Canada ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-canada/)

## Frequently asked questions

Why is exenatide hard to find?

Newer once-weekly options largely replaced it, and the manufacturer has wound down US supply.

# Soliqua 100/33

insulin glargine + lixisenatide · Basal insulin + GLP-1 receptor agonist combination · Sanofi
✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

In short
**Soliqua** (insulin glargine + lixisenatide) is a basal insulin + GLP-1 receptor agonist combination made by Sanofi, used for blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes. Schedule: once daily. It is prescription-only in the US and Canada.

**Form**Prefilled pen
**How often**Once daily

**United States**FDA-approved. Standalone lixisenatide (Adlyxin) has been discontinued; lixisenatide remains available inside Soliqua.
**Canada**Check the Drug Product Database.
**Prescription**Required

## What it is used for

- Blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes

## Soliqua dosage

Per the official label. Your prescriber sets your dose — never change it on your own.

| 1Dose | Set in units by your prescriber based on prior therapy and blood sugar; injected within the hour before the first meal of the day |

### How to take it

Once daily within 1 hour before the first meal.
### Storage

Refrigerate before use; after first use, room temperature up to 28 days.

## Side effects

### Common

- Nausea
- Diarrhea
- Vomiting
- Constipation
- Abdominal pain
- Indigestion / heartburn
- Fatigue
- Decreased appetite

### Serious — get medical help

- Pancreatitis (severe stomach pain that may spread to the back)
- Gallbladder problems, including gallstones
- Low blood sugar when combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea
- Kidney problems, often from dehydration after vomiting or diarrhea
- Serious allergic reactions
- Diabetic retinopathy complications (people with type 2 diabetes)
- Pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation — tell your surgical team you take it
### Who should not use it

- Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, or MEN 2
- Prior serious allergic reaction to the drug or its ingredients
- Pregnancy (stop before a planned pregnancy as advised by your prescriber)
- Use together with another GLP-1 receptor agonist

## Cost

Brand-only; check manufacturer savings programs.

## How to buy Soliqua legally

- Get a prescription from your doctor or a licensed telehealth provider.

- Fill it at a licensed pharmacy.

- Verify any online pharmacy first (US: [safe.pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/); Canada: your provincial pharmacy college register).

[Buying legally in the USA ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-usa/) [Buying legally in Canada ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-canada/)

## Frequently asked questions

Does Soliqua have the thyroid boxed warning?

No. Lixisenatide-containing products do not carry that boxed warning, though general GLP-1 precautions still apply.

# Xultophy 100/3.6

insulin degludec + liraglutide · Basal insulin + GLP-1 receptor agonist combination · Novo Nordisk
✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

In short
**Xultophy** (insulin degludec + liraglutide) is a basal insulin + GLP-1 receptor agonist combination made by Novo Nordisk, used for blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes. Schedule: once daily. It is prescription-only in the US and Canada.

**Form**Prefilled pen
**How often**Once daily

**United States**FDA-approved.
**Canada**Check the Drug Product Database.
**Prescription**Required
**⚠ Boxed warning: risk of thyroid C-cell tumors. Do not use if you or a family member has had medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) or if you have Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia syndrome type 2 (MEN 2).**

## What it is used for

- Blood sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes

## Xultophy dosage

Per the official label. Your prescriber sets your dose — never change it on your own.

| 1Dose | Set in units by your prescriber; injected at the same time each day |

### How to take it

Once daily, same time each day, with or without food.
### Storage

Refrigerate before use; after first use, up to 21 days at room temperature or in the fridge.

## Side effects

### Common

- Nausea
- Diarrhea
- Vomiting
- Constipation
- Abdominal pain
- Indigestion / heartburn
- Fatigue
- Decreased appetite

### Serious — get medical help

- Pancreatitis (severe stomach pain that may spread to the back)
- Gallbladder problems, including gallstones
- Low blood sugar when combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea
- Kidney problems, often from dehydration after vomiting or diarrhea
- Serious allergic reactions
- Diabetic retinopathy complications (people with type 2 diabetes)
- Pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation — tell your surgical team you take it
### Who should not use it

- Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, or MEN 2
- Prior serious allergic reaction to the drug or its ingredients
- Pregnancy (stop before a planned pregnancy as advised by your prescriber)
- Use together with another GLP-1 receptor agonist

## Cost

Brand-only; check manufacturer programs.
[GLP-1 cost without insurance ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/glp1-cost-without-insurance/)

## How to buy Xultophy legally

- Get a prescription from your doctor or a licensed telehealth provider.

- Fill it at a licensed pharmacy, or through the manufacturer's self-pay pharmacy.

- Verify any online pharmacy first (US: [safe.pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/); Canada: your provincial pharmacy college register).

[Buying legally in the USA ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-usa/) [Buying legally in Canada ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-canada/)

## Frequently asked questions

Can Xultophy be combined with another GLP-1?

No. It already contains liraglutide.
**Also searched as:** insulin degludec and liraglutide, Xultophy pen, IDegLira

## Sources

- [FDA prescribing information (DailyMed)](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?query=Xultophy)

- [Drugs@FDA](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/daf/)

- [Health Canada Drug Product Database](https://health-products.canada.ca/dpd-bdpp/)

Insulins
# Insulin lispro: Humalog, Admelog, Lyumjev

insulin lispro · Rapid-acting (mealtime) insulin · Eli Lilly; Sanofi (Admelog)
✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

In short
**Insulin lispro** (insulin lispro) is a rapid-acting (mealtime) insulin made by Eli Lilly; Sanofi (Admelog), used for mealtime blood sugar control in type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Schedule: with meals. It is prescription-only in the US and Canada.

**Form**Vials, pens, cartridges
**How often**With meals

**United States**FDA-approved; lower-cost unbranded lispro is available.
**Canada**Available in Canada.
**Prescription**Required

## What it is used for

- Mealtime blood sugar control in type 1 and type 2 diabetes

## Insulin lispro dosage

Per the official label. Your prescriber sets your dose — never change it on your own.

| 1Dose | Individualized in units by your prescriber |
| 2Timing | Humalog/Admelog: within 15 minutes before or right after a meal. Lyumjev: at the start of a meal or within 20 minutes after starting |

### How to take it

Under the skin; some forms are also used in insulin pumps.
### Storage

Unopened: refrigerate. In use: room temperature up to 28 days.

## Side effects

### Common

- Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)
- Injection-site reactions
- Weight gain
- Lipodystrophy or skin thickening at repeated injection sites

### Serious — get medical help

- Severe hypoglycemia (confusion, seizures, loss of consciousness)
- Low potassium (hypokalemia)
- Fluid retention and heart failure when combined with thiazolidinediones
- Serious allergic reactions
### Who should not use it

- During an episode of low blood sugar
- Never share pens or needles, even if the needle is changed
- Do not switch insulin type, brand or concentration without your prescriber

## Cost

US insulin out-of-pocket costs are capped at $35/month for Medicare; manufacturers offer $35 programs for many patients. Verify eligibility.
[GLP-1 cost without insurance ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/glp1-cost-without-insurance/)

## How to buy Insulin lispro legally

- Get a prescription from your doctor or a licensed telehealth provider.

- Fill it at a licensed pharmacy, or through the manufacturer's self-pay pharmacy.

- Verify any online pharmacy first (US: [safe.pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/); Canada: your provincial pharmacy college register).

[Buying legally in the USA ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-usa/) [Buying legally in Canada ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-canada/)

## Common questions

- [How to use an insulin pen](https://www.glpatlas.com/questions/how-to-use-insulin-pen/)

## Frequently asked questions

Is Lyumjev faster than Humalog?

Yes. Lyumjev contains ingredients that speed absorption, so it starts working sooner.
**Also searched as:** Humalog, Admelog, Lyumjev, Humalog KwikPen, lispro, mealtime insulin, rapid-acting insulin

## Sources

- [FDA prescribing information (DailyMed)](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/search.cfm?query=Insulin+lispro)

- [Drugs@FDA](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/scripts/cder/daf/)

- [Health Canada Drug Product Database](https://health-products.canada.ca/dpd-bdpp/)

## Related

# Insulin aspart: NovoLog, Fiasp

insulin aspart · Rapid-acting (mealtime) insulin · Novo Nordisk
✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

In short
**Insulin aspart** (insulin aspart) is a rapid-acting (mealtime) insulin made by Novo Nordisk, used for mealtime blood sugar control in type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Schedule: with meals. It is prescription-only in the US and Canada.

**Form**Vials, pens, cartridges
**How often**With meals

**United States**FDA-approved; unbranded insulin aspart is available.
**Canada**Available in Canada (NovoRapid, Fiasp).
**Prescription**Required

## What it is used for

- Mealtime blood sugar control in type 1 and type 2 diabetes

## Insulin aspart dosage

Per the official label. Your prescriber sets your dose — never change it on your own.

| 1Dose | Individualized in units by your prescriber |
| 2Timing | NovoLog: 5–10 minutes before a meal. Fiasp: at the start of a meal or within 20 minutes after starting |

### How to take it

Under the skin; also used in pumps.
### Storage

Unopened: refrigerate. In use: room temperature up to 28 days.

## Side effects

### Common

- Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)
- Injection-site reactions
- Weight gain
- Lipodystrophy or skin thickening at repeated injection sites

### Serious — get medical help

- Severe hypoglycemia (confusion, seizures, loss of consciousness)
- Low potassium (hypokalemia)
- Fluid retention and heart failure when combined with thiazolidinediones
- Serious allergic reactions
### Who should not use it

- During an episode of low blood sugar
- Never share pens or needles, even if the needle is changed
- Do not switch insulin type, brand or concentration without your prescriber

## Cost

See $35 insulin programs and Medicare caps.

# Regular (short-acting) insulin: Humulin R, Novolin R

human insulin (regular) · Short-acting insulin · Eli Lilly; Novo Nordisk
✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

In short
**Regular insulin** (human insulin (regular)) is a short-acting insulin made by Eli Lilly; Novo Nordisk, used for blood sugar control in diabetes. Schedule: before meals. It is prescription-only in the US and Canada.

**Form**Vials, pens
**How often**Before meals

**United States**FDA-approved. U-100 is sold over the counter at many US pharmacies; Humulin R U-500 requires a prescription.
**Canada**Available in Canada.
**Prescription**Required

## What it is used for

- Blood sugar control in diabetes

## Regular insulin dosage

Per the official label. Your prescriber sets your dose — never change it on your own.

| 1Dose | Individualized in units |
| 2Timing | About 30 minutes before a meal |

### How to take it

Under the skin.
### Storage

Unopened: refrigerate. In use: per product labeling (often 31–42 days).

## Side effects

### Common

- Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)
- Injection-site reactions
- Weight gain
- Lipodystrophy or skin thickening at repeated injection sites

### Serious — get medical help

- Severe hypoglycemia (confusion, seizures, loss of consciousness)
- Low potassium (hypokalemia)
- Fluid retention and heart failure when combined with thiazolidinediones
- Serious allergic reactions
### Who should not use it

- During an episode of low blood sugar
- Never share pens or needles, even if the needle is changed
- Do not switch insulin type, brand or concentration without your prescriber

## Cost

Among the lowest-cost insulins in the US.
[GLP-1 cost without insurance ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/glp1-cost-without-insurance/)

## How to buy Regular insulin legally

- Get a prescription from your doctor or a licensed telehealth provider.

- Fill it at a licensed pharmacy, or through the manufacturer's self-pay pharmacy.

- Verify any online pharmacy first (US: [safe.pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/); Canada: your provincial pharmacy college register).

[Buying legally in the USA ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-usa/) [Buying legally in Canada ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-canada/)

## Frequently asked questions

Is U-500 the same as U-100?

No. U-500 is five times more concentrated and must only be used with its dedicated pen or U-500 syringe.
**Also searched as:** Humulin R, Novolin R, regular insulin, short-acting insulin, U-500 insulin, over the counter insulin

# NPH (intermediate-acting) insulin: Humulin N, Novolin N

isophane human insulin · Intermediate-acting insulin · Eli Lilly; Novo Nordisk
✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

In short
**NPH insulin** (isophane human insulin) is an intermediate-acting insulin made by Eli Lilly; Novo Nordisk, used for basal blood sugar control in diabetes. Schedule: once or twice daily. It is prescription-only in the US and Canada.

**Form**Vials, pens
**How often**Once or twice daily

**United States**FDA-approved; available over the counter at many US pharmacies.
**Canada**Available in Canada.
**Prescription**Required

## What it is used for

- Basal blood sugar control in diabetes

## NPH insulin dosage

Per the official label. Your prescriber sets your dose — never change it on your own.

| 1Dose | Individualized in units |

### How to take it

Roll gently to resuspend (cloudy insulin) before each injection; do not shake hard.
### Storage

Unopened: refrigerate. In use: per labeling.

## Side effects

### Common

- Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)
- Injection-site reactions
- Weight gain
- Lipodystrophy or skin thickening at repeated injection sites

### Serious — get medical help

- Severe hypoglycemia (confusion, seizures, loss of consciousness)
- Low potassium (hypokalemia)
- Fluid retention and heart failure when combined with thiazolidinediones
- Serious allergic reactions
### Who should not use it

- During an episode of low blood sugar
- Never share pens or needles, even if the needle is changed
- Do not switch insulin type, brand or concentration without your prescriber

## Cost

Low-cost option.

# Insulin glargine: Lantus, Basaglar, Semglee, Rezvoglar, Toujeo

insulin glargine · Long-acting (basal) insulin · Sanofi; Eli Lilly; Biocon/Viatris
✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

In short
**Insulin glargine** (insulin glargine) is a long-acting (basal) insulin made by Sanofi; Eli Lilly; Biocon/Viatris, used for basal blood sugar control in type 1 and type 2 diabetes. Schedule: once daily. It is prescription-only in the US and Canada.

**Form**Vials, pens
**How often**Once daily

**United States**FDA-approved. Semglee and Rezvoglar are interchangeable biosimilars to Lantus. Toujeo is a concentrated U-300 form. Levemir (insulin detemir) has been discontinued in the US.
**Canada**Available in Canada (including biosimilars).
**Prescription**Required

## What it is used for

- Basal blood sugar control in type 1 and type 2 diabetes

## Insulin glargine dosage

Per the official label. Your prescriber sets your dose — never change it on your own.

| 1Dose | Individualized in units, same time each day |
| 2Toujeo | U-300 concentration — not unit-for-unit identical to U-100 glargine when switching |

### How to take it

Under the skin once daily. Do not dilute or mix with other insulins.
### Storage

Unopened: refrigerate. In use: Lantus up to 28 days; Toujeo up to 56 days.

## Side effects

### Common

- Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)
- Injection-site reactions
- Weight gain
- Lipodystrophy or skin thickening at repeated injection sites

### Serious — get medical help

- Severe hypoglycemia (confusion, seizures, loss of consciousness)
- Low potassium (hypokalemia)
- Fluid retention and heart failure when combined with thiazolidinediones
- Serious allergic reactions
### Who should not use it

- During an episode of low blood sugar
- Never share pens or needles, even if the needle is changed
- Do not switch insulin type, brand or concentration without your prescriber

## Cost

Biosimilars and $35 programs lower costs.
[GLP-1 cost without insurance ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/glp1-cost-without-insurance/)

## How to buy Insulin glargine legally

- Get a prescription from your doctor or a licensed telehealth provider.

- Fill it at a licensed pharmacy.

- Verify any online pharmacy first (US: [safe.pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/); Canada: your provincial pharmacy college register).

[Buying legally in the USA ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-usa/) [Buying legally in Canada ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-canada/)

## Common questions

- [Signs of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)](https://www.glpatlas.com/questions/hypoglycemia-signs/)
- [How to use an insulin pen](https://www.glpatlas.com/questions/how-to-use-insulin-pen/)

## Frequently asked questions

What replaced Levemir?

After Levemir's US discontinuation, people were moved to other basal insulins such as glargine or degludec by their prescribers.
**Also searched as:** Lantus, Basaglar, Semglee, Rezvoglar, Toujeo, Lantus SoloStar, long-acting insulin, basal insulin, Levemir replacement, insulin glargine biosimilar

# Insulin degludec: Tresiba

insulin degludec · Ultra-long-acting (basal) insulin · Novo Nordisk
✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

In short
**Tresiba** (insulin degludec) is an ultra-long-acting (basal) insulin made by Novo Nordisk, used for basal blood sugar control in diabetes (adults and children 1+). Schedule: once daily. It is prescription-only in the US and Canada.

**Form**Pens (U-100, U-200), vials
**How often**Once daily

**United States**FDA-approved; unbranded insulin degludec is available.
**Canada**Available in Canada.
**Prescription**Required

## What it is used for

- Basal blood sugar control in diabetes (adults and children 1+)

## Tresiba dosage

Per the official label. Your prescriber sets your dose — never change it on your own.

| 1Dose | Individualized in units; flexible timing, at least 8 hours between doses |

### How to take it

Under the skin once daily.
### Storage

Unopened: refrigerate. In use: up to 56 days.

## Side effects

### Common

- Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)
- Injection-site reactions
- Weight gain
- Lipodystrophy or skin thickening at repeated injection sites

### Serious — get medical help

- Severe hypoglycemia (confusion, seizures, loss of consciousness)
- Low potassium (hypokalemia)
- Fluid retention and heart failure when combined with thiazolidinediones
- Serious allergic reactions
### Who should not use it

- During an episode of low blood sugar
- Never share pens or needles, even if the needle is changed
- Do not switch insulin type, brand or concentration without your prescriber

## Cost

See $35 programs.
[GLP-1 cost without insurance ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/glp1-cost-without-insurance/)

## How to buy Tresiba legally

- Get a prescription from your doctor or a licensed telehealth provider.

- Fill it at a licensed pharmacy, or through the manufacturer's self-pay pharmacy.

- Verify any online pharmacy first (US: [safe.pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/); Canada: your provincial pharmacy college register).

[Buying legally in the USA ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-usa/) [Buying legally in Canada ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-canada/)

**Also searched as:** Tresiba, degludec, Tresiba FlexTouch, ultra long-acting insulin

Other diabetes injectables
# Symlin

pramlintide · Amylin analog · AstraZeneca
✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

In short
**Symlin** (pramlintide) is an amylin analog made by AstraZeneca, used for added to mealtime insulin in type 1 or type 2 diabetes. Schedule: before major meals. It is prescription-only in the US and Canada.

**Form**Pen injection
**How often**Before major meals

**United States**FDA-approved.
**Canada**Not marketed in Canada as far as public listings show; check the Drug Product Database.
**Prescription**Required
**⚠ Boxed warning: severe low blood sugar with insulin, especially in type 1 diabetes.**

## What it is used for

- Added to mealtime insulin in type 1 or type 2 diabetes

## Symlin dosage

Per the official label. Your prescriber sets your dose — never change it on your own.

| 1Dose | Titrated in micrograms by your prescriber; mealtime insulin is usually reduced at the start |

### How to take it

Inject before major meals; never mix with insulin.
### Storage

Refrigerate before use; in use up to 30 days.

## Side effects

### Common

- Nausea
- Diarrhea
- Vomiting
- Constipation
- Abdominal pain
- Indigestion / heartburn
- Fatigue
- Decreased appetite

### Serious — get medical help

- Pancreatitis (severe stomach pain that may spread to the back)
- Gallbladder problems, including gallstones
- Low blood sugar when combined with insulin or a sulfonylurea
- Kidney problems, often from dehydration after vomiting or diarrhea
- Serious allergic reactions
- Diabetic retinopathy complications (people with type 2 diabetes)
- Pulmonary aspiration during anesthesia or deep sedation — tell your surgical team you take it
### Who should not use it

- Personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, or MEN 2
- Prior serious allergic reaction to the drug or its ingredients
- Pregnancy (stop before a planned pregnancy as advised by your prescriber)
- Use together with another GLP-1 receptor agonist

## Cost

Brand-only.
[GLP-1 cost without insurance ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/glp1-cost-without-insurance/)

## How to buy Symlin legally

- Get a prescription from your doctor or a licensed telehealth provider.

- Fill it at a licensed pharmacy.

- Verify any online pharmacy first (US: [safe.pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/); Canada: your provincial pharmacy college register).

[Buying legally in the USA ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-usa/) [Buying legally in Canada ](https://www.glpatlas.com/guides/how-to-buy-glp1-legally-canada/)

**Also searched as:** pramlintide, SymlinPen, amylin

Title: Ozempic vs Wegovy: same drug, different jobs

Comparison
# Ozempic vs Wegovy: same drug, different jobs

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Quick answer
Ozempic and Wegovy both contain semaglutide. Compare approvals, doses, pills vs pens and cost in the US and Canada. The choice is usually made by the diagnosis, not by preference: a person with type 2 diabetes is typically prescribed Ozempic, while a person treated for weight is prescribed Wegovy. Insurers apply different coverage rules to each, which is why the same molecule can cost very different amounts.

## Side by side

| Feature | Ozempic | Wegovy |
| Active ingredient | Semaglutide | Semaglutide |
| Approved for | Type 2 diabetes (plus heart and kidney risk reduction) | Weight management, heart risk reduction, MASH |
| Highest dose | 2 mg weekly | 2.4 mg weekly; 7.2 mg as Wegovy HD |
| Pill version | Ozempic tablets (1.5/4/9 mg) | Wegovy pill (up to 25 mg) |
| Generic in Canada | Yes (2026) | Yes, for weight management (June 2026) |

## Which one is right for you?

The choice is usually made by the diagnosis, not by preference: a person with type 2 diabetes is typically prescribed Ozempic, while a person treated for weight is prescribed Wegovy. Insurers apply different coverage rules to each, which is why the same molecule can cost very different amounts.
Both are prescription medicines. Which one fits depends on your diagnosis, history and coverage — decide with your prescriber.

# Wegovy vs Zepbound: semaglutide vs tirzepatide for weight loss

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Quick answer
Wegovy (semaglutide) vs Zepbound (tirzepatide): weight-loss results, dosing, side effects and self-pay costs compared. In head-to-head research tirzepatide produced greater average weight loss than semaglutide 2.4 mg. Wegovy HD narrows that gap. Side effects are similar and mostly gastrointestinal.

## Side by side

| Feature | Wegovy | Zepbound |
| Molecule | Semaglutide (GLP-1) | Tirzepatide (GIP + GLP-1) |
| Dosing | Weekly; up to 2.4 mg or 7.2 mg (HD) | Weekly; up to 15 mg |
| Extra approvals | Heart risk reduction, MASH | Obstructive sleep apnea |
| Oral option | Wegovy pill | None (Lilly's oral is Foundayo, a different drug) |
| Self-pay channel | NovoCare & partner pharmacies | LillyDirect (vials and pens) |

## Which one is right for you?

In head-to-head research tirzepatide produced greater average weight loss than semaglutide 2.4 mg. Wegovy HD narrows that gap. Side effects are similar and mostly gastrointestinal.
Both are prescription medicines. Which one fits depends on your diagnosis, history and coverage — decide with your prescriber.

# Wegovy pill vs Foundayo: the two weight-loss pills compared

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

The Wegovy pill (oral semaglutide) and Foundayo (orforglipron) compared: how to take them, results, doses and cost. The Wegovy pill showed larger average weight loss in trials; Foundayo is easier to take because it has no fasting rule. Both carry the thyroid C-cell boxed warning.

## Side by side

| Feature | Wegovy pill | Foundayo |
| Molecule | Semaglutide (peptide) | Orforglipron (small molecule) |

| How to take | Fasting, ≤4 oz water, wait 30 min | Any time, with or without food |
| Maintenance dose | 25 mg daily | 5.5 to 17.2 mg daily |
| Avg. weight loss in trials | Comparable to Wegovy 2.4 mg injection | About 12% at highest dose (72 weeks) |

## Which one is right for you?

The Wegovy pill showed larger average weight loss in trials; Foundayo is easier to take because it has no fasting rule. Both carry the thyroid C-cell boxed warning.
Both are prescription medicines. Which one fits depends on your diagnosis, history and coverage — decide with your prescriber.

Title: How to buy GLP-1 medicines legally in the USA

Guide
# How to buy GLP-1 medicines legally in the USA

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
The legal ways to buy or order Wegovy, Zepbound, Ozempic, Mounjaro and GLP-1 pills in the US — prescriptions, pharmacies, telehealth and direct-from-manufacturer.

Key point
Every GLP-1 medicine is prescription-only in the US. There is no legal way to purchase them without a valid prescription from a licensed prescriber.

## Step 1: Get a prescription

From your own doctor or from a telehealth service whose prescribers are licensed in your state. A real consultation reviews your medical history, current medicines and any personal or family history of thyroid cancer.

## Step 2: Choose where to fill it

- **Your local or mail-order pharmacy**, billed to insurance when covered.

- **Direct-from-manufacturer self-pay**: NovoCare Pharmacy (Wegovy, Ozempic, Wegovy pill) and LillyDirect (Zepbound, Mounjaro, Foundayo).

- **Telehealth programs** that send prescriptions to licensed pharmacies.

## Step 3: Check the pharmacy is legitimate

Use the NABP's [safe.pharmacy](https://safe.pharmacy/) lookup. Legitimate online pharmacies require a prescription, are licensed in your state and have a US address.

## Red flags

- No prescription required
- "Research use only" peptides or powders
- Payment by crypto, gift card or wire only
- Ordering through WhatsApp or social media DMs
- Pens labeled for another country

In August 2026 the FDA issued warning letters to online sellers of products marketed as semaglutide, tirzepatide and retatrutide. Foreign-labeled pens are unapproved in the US even when genuine.

Guide
# How to buy GLP-1 medicines legally in Canada

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
How to get Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro and generic semaglutide legally in Canada: prescriptions, pharmacies, coverage and the new generics.

Key point
In Canada, GLP-1 medicines are prescription drugs dispensed by provincially licensed pharmacies.

## Get a prescription

From a family doctor, nurse practitioner, or a licensed virtual-care provider in your province.

## Generic semaglutide is here

Health Canada authorized the first generic semaglutide (Ozempic equivalent) on April 28, 2026 and a second on May 1, 2026, and the first generic for weight management on June 29, 2026. Ask your pharmacist whether a generic can be substituted under your plan and province.

## Verify the pharmacy

Every pharmacy must be licensed by its provincial regulatory college. Look it up on your college's public register before ordering online.

## Coverage

Provincial plans and private insurers set their own rules; many require prior authorization. Obesity coverage is often an optional benefit.

Guide
# Compounded, research-peptide and counterfeit GLP-1s: the risks

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Why compounded, 'research' and counterfeit semaglutide and tirzepatide are risky, and how to spot fake Ozempic and Wegovy pens.

Key point
Compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide are not FDA-approved. Products sold as "research peptides" are not meant for humans at all. Counterfeit pens of Ozempic and other GLP-1s have been found in the US and abroad.

## How to protect yourself

- Fill prescriptions only at licensed pharmacies.
- Check pen labels, lot numbers and expiry dates; report anything odd to the pharmacist.
- Never buy from social media sellers, WhatsApp vendors or sites that don't need a prescription.
- Report suspected fakes to FDA MedWatch (US) or Health Canada.

Sellers of these products face FDA warning letters and lawsuits from Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly.

Title: GLP-1 side effects: what's common, what's serious
Summary: Common and serious side effects of semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide and orforglipron, and when to call a doctor.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Guide
# GLP-1 side effects: what's common, what's serious

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Common and serious side effects of semaglutide, tirzepatide, liraglutide and orforglipron, and when to call a doctor.

Key point
Most side effects are digestive and appear when starting or increasing the dose: nausea, diarrhea, vomiting, constipation and stomach pain. Slow dose increases are designed to limit them.

## Get medical help for

- Severe stomach pain that does not go away, with or without vomiting (possible pancreatitis)
- Pain in the upper right abdomen, fever, yellow skin or eyes (gallbladder)
- Signs of dehydration or reduced urine
- A lump or swelling in the neck, hoarseness, trouble swallowing
- Signs of a serious allergic reaction

Tell any surgical or endoscopy team that you take a GLP-1 medicine, because of the risk of aspiration under anesthesia.

# New GLP-1 drugs coming: the 2026–2027 pipeline

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
CagriSema, retatrutide and other upcoming obesity and diabetes drugs: status, results and expected decisions.

Key point
None of the investigational products is legally sold. Anything marketed as one online is unapproved.

- **CagriSema** (Novo Nordisk): filed with the FDA December 2025; decision expected Q4 2026.

- **Retatrutide** (Lilly): triple agonist; FDA submission planned for Q1 2027 after positive phase 3 results.

- **Ozempic tablets 25 mg**: under FDA review, decision expected by end of 2026.

- **Survodutide** (Boehringer Ingelheim / Zealand Pharma) and other agents remain in development.

# Semaglutide — the complete guide

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Semaglutide explained: Ozempic, Wegovy, Wegovy HD, Wegovy pill and Ozempic tablets — uses, doses, side effects, generics and cost in the US and Canada.

In short
Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist made by Novo Nordisk. It mimics a gut hormone that raises insulin release after meals, lowers glucagon, slows stomach emptying and reduces appetite.

## Semaglutide brands

| Brand | Form | Approved for (US) |

| Ozempic | Weekly injection, 0.25–2 mg | Type 2 diabetes; heart and kidney risk reduction |

| Ozempic tablets (formerly Rybelsus) | Daily tablet, 1.5/4/9 mg | Type 2 diabetes |

| Wegovy / Wegovy HD | Weekly injection, up to 2.4 mg or 7.2 mg | Weight management; heart risk; MASH |

| Wegovy pill | Daily tablet, up to 25 mg | Weight management |

## Is there generic semaglutide?

In Canada, yes — Health Canada authorized generics in April, May and June 2026. In the US, no FDA-approved generic exists; key patents run into the early 2030s. Compounded and "research" semaglutide are not approved products.

## How long does semaglutide stay in your body?

Its half-life is about one week, so it takes roughly five weeks after the last weekly dose to leave the body.

Title: Tirzepatide: Mounjaro and Zepbound explained (2026)
Summary: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound): how the dual GIP/GLP-1 drug works, doses, results, side effects, vials vs pens and cost.

Topic
# Tirzepatide — Mounjaro and Zepbound

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Tirzepatide (Mounjaro, Zepbound): how the dual GIP/GLP-1 drug works, doses, results, side effects, vials vs pens and cost.

In short
Tirzepatide, made by Eli Lilly, activates two gut-hormone receptors — GIP and GLP-1. It is sold as [Mounjaro](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/mounjaro/) for type 2 diabetes and [Zepbound](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/zepbound/) for weight management and obstructive sleep apnea in the US.

## Doses

Both start at 2.5 mg weekly for 4 weeks, rise to 5 mg, then by 2.5 mg steps every 4 weeks or more, up to 15 mg weekly.

## Tirzepatide vs semaglutide

In head-to-head research tirzepatide produced more average weight loss than semaglutide 2.4 mg. See [Wegovy vs Zepbound](https://www.glpatlas.com/compare/wegovy-vs-zepbound/).

## Birth control

Tirzepatide can make oral contraceptives less effective. The label advises switching to a non-oral method or adding a barrier method for 4 weeks after starting and for 4 weeks after each dose increase.

## Medicines in this group

[GLP-1 & incretin medicinesMounjarotirzepatide · Once weekly](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/mounjaro/)[GLP-1 & incretin medicinesZepboundtirzepatide · Once weekly](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/zepbound/)[PipelineRetatrutide (investigational)retatrutide · Once weekly](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/retatrutide/)

# Diabetes injections — every option

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Complete list of diabetes injections in 2026: GLP-1s (Ozempic, Mounjaro, Trulicity, Victoza), insulins (Lantus, Humalog, Tresiba, Awiqli), combinations and glucagon.

In short
Weekly: [Ozempic](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/ozempic/), [Mounjaro](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/mounjaro/), [Trulicity](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/trulicity/), Bydureon BCise. Daily: [Victoza / liraglutide](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/victoza/). These lower blood sugar and often body weight, with low risk of hypoglycemia on their own.
## Non-insulin injections (GLP-1 and dual agonists)

## Insulins

Basal (long-acting): [glargine](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/insulin-glargine/), [degludec](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/insulin-degludec/), and the once-weekly [Awiqli](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/insulin-icodec/). Mealtime: [lispro](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/insulin-lispro/), [aspart](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/insulin-aspart/), [glulisine](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/insulin-glulisine/). Human insulins: [regular](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/regular-insulin/), [NPH](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/nph-insulin/), [premixed](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/premixed-insulin/).

## Combinations

[Soliqua](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/soliqua/) (glargine + lixisenatide) and [Xultophy](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/xultophy/) (degludec + liraglutide).

## Other

[Symlin](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/symlin/) (pramlintide) with mealtime insulin, and [glucagon](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/glucagon/) for emergencies.

Title: Weight loss injections and pills approved in 2026
Summary: Every FDA-approved weight loss injection and GLP-1 pill in 2026: Wegovy, Wegovy HD, Zepbound, Saxenda, Wegovy pill and Foundayo — results, doses and cost.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Topic
# Weight loss injections and pills

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
Every FDA-approved weight loss injection and GLP-1 pill in 2026: Wegovy, Wegovy HD, Zepbound, Saxenda, Wegovy pill and Foundayo — results, doses and cost.

In short
Ozempic and Mounjaro are diabetes brands; prescribing them for weight loss is off-label. CagriSema and retatrutide are not approved.
| Medicine | Type | How often |

| Zepbound | Tirzepatide injection | Weekly |

| Wegovy / Wegovy HD | Semaglutide injection | Weekly |

| Saxenda (generic available) | Liraglutide injection | Daily |

| Wegovy pill | Oral semaglutide | Daily, fasting |

| Foundayo | Orforglipron tablet | Daily, any time |

## Who qualifies?

US labels cover adults with a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 or more with a weight-related condition such as high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes or high cholesterol. Some products are also approved for adolescents.

# Insulin — types, brands and how they differ

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)
All insulin types explained: rapid, short, intermediate, long-acting, once-weekly and premixed — brands, timing, storage and $35 cost programs.

In short
Never switch insulin type, brand or concentration without your prescriber.
| Type | Examples | Role |

| Rapid-acting | Humalog, Admelog, Lyumjev, NovoLog, Fiasp, Apidra | Mealtime |

| Short-acting | Humulin R, Novolin R | Mealtime |

| Intermediate | Humulin N, Novolin N | Basal |

| Long-acting | Lantus, Basaglar, Semglee, Rezvoglar, Toujeo, Tresiba | Basal, daily |

| Once-weekly | Awiqli (US approval March 2026) | Basal, weekly |

| Premixed | Humalog Mix 75/25, NovoLog Mix 70/30, 70/30 | Basal + mealtime |

Title: What if I miss an Ozempic dose?
Summary: Take it as soon as possible within 5 days of the missed dose. If more than 5 days have passed, skip it and take the next dose on your usual day. Never…
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Question
# What if I miss an Ozempic dose?

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
Take it as soon as possible within 5 days of the missed dose. If more than 5 days have passed, skip it and take the next dose on your usual day. Never take two doses to catch up.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.

Title: What if I miss a Wegovy dose?
Summary: If the next scheduled dose is more than 2 days away, take the missed dose as soon as possible. If it is less than 2 days away, skip it. If you miss more…
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Question
# What if I miss a Wegovy dose?

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
If the next scheduled dose is more than 2 days away, take the missed dose as soon as possible. If it is less than 2 days away, skip it. If you miss more than 2 weeks, contact your prescriber — you may need to restart at a lower dose.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.

Title: Can you drink alcohol on Ozempic, Wegovy or Zepbound?
Summary: The labels do not ban alcohol, but alcohol can worsen nausea and, with insulin or sulfonylureas, raise the risk of low blood sugar. Heavy drinking also…
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Question
# Can you drink alcohol on Ozempic, Wegovy or Zepbound?

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
The labels do not ban alcohol, but alcohol can worsen nausea and, with insulin or sulfonylureas, raise the risk of low blood sugar. Heavy drinking also raises pancreatitis risk. Ask your prescriber what is safe for you.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.

Question
# How long does semaglutide stay in your system?

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
Semaglutide has a half-life of about one week, so it takes about five weeks after the last weekly injection to leave the body. Effects on appetite fade over that period.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.

Question
# What is 'Ozempic face'?

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
A popular term for a hollow or aged facial look after rapid weight loss. It is caused by loss of facial fat, not by a direct effect of the drug, and can happen with any large weight loss.

Question
# Does Wegovy or Zepbound cause hair loss?

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Question
# What happens when you stop Wegovy or Zepbound?

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
Appetite returns over a few weeks and most people regain a large share of lost weight within a year, as shown in withdrawal studies. Blood sugar may rise in people with diabetes. Plan any stop with your prescriber.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.

Question
# Can you take Ozempic or Wegovy while pregnant or trying to conceive?

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
No. Semaglutide should be stopped at least 2 months before a planned pregnancy because of its long half-life. Tirzepatide can reduce oral contraceptive effectiveness. Talk to your prescriber before trying to conceive.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.

Question
# Where do you inject Ozempic, Wegovy or Zepbound?

# How to manage nausea and constipation on GLP-1 medicines

Title: What is a GLP-1 agonist?
Summary: A medicine that mimics glucagon-like peptide-1, a gut hormone released after eating. GLP-1 agonists raise insulin when blood sugar is high, lower…
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Question
# What is a GLP-1 agonist?

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
A medicine that mimics glucagon-like peptide-1, a gut hormone released after eating. GLP-1 agonists raise insulin when blood sugar is high, lower glucagon, slow stomach emptying and reduce appetite. Examples: semaglutide, liraglutide, dulaglutide; tirzepatide also acts on GIP.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.

Title: Semaglutide vs tirzepatide: which is stronger?
Summary: Tirzepatide (Zepbound, Mounjaro) produced more average weight loss than semaglutide 2.4 mg (Wegovy) in head-to-head research. Semaglutide has more labeled…
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Question
# Semaglutide vs tirzepatide: which is stronger?

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
Tirzepatide (Zepbound, Mounjaro) produced more average weight loss than semaglutide 2.4 mg (Wegovy) in head-to-head research. Semaglutide has more labeled outcome indications (heart, kidney, MASH). Wegovy HD 7.2 mg narrows the gap.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.

Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Question
# How to spot fake Ozempic or Wegovy pens

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
Buy only from licensed pharmacies, check that the label, lot number and expiry are intact and match the box, and report anything unusual. Pens sold without a prescription, through social media or WhatsApp, or labeled for another country are red flags. Report suspected fakes to FDA MedWatch or Health Canada.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.
