Title: Is compounded semaglutide legal?
Summary: Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved. Since the FDA removed semaglutide and tirzepatide from its shortage list, routine copying of the approved products…
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Question
# Is compounded semaglutide legal?

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
Compounded drugs are not FDA-approved. Since the FDA removed semaglutide and tirzepatide from its shortage list, routine copying of the approved products by compounders is restricted, and the FDA has issued warning letters to sellers. 'Research use only' products are not for human use.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.

Title: How long does it take for Wegovy or Zepbound to work?
Summary: Appetite often changes within the first weeks, but the starting doses are for tolerance, not full effect. Most weight loss happens over months as the dose…
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Question
# How long does it take for Wegovy or Zepbound to work?

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
Appetite often changes within the first weeks, but the starting doses are for tolerance, not full effect. Most weight loss happens over months as the dose rises; trials measured results at about 68–72 weeks.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.

# What to eat on GLP-1 medicines

Title: How to store and travel with GLP-1 pens
Summary: Keep unopened pens refrigerated (36–46°F / 2–8°C), never frozen. In use, most pens tolerate room temperature for a limited time (Ozempic up to 56 days;…
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Question
# How to store and travel with GLP-1 pens

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
Keep unopened pens refrigerated (36–46°F / 2–8°C), never frozen. In use, most pens tolerate room temperature for a limited time (Ozempic up to 56 days; Wegovy up to 28 days; Zepbound and Mounjaro up to 21 days). Carry them in hand luggage with the prescription label.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.

Title: Signs of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)
Summary: Shakiness, sweating, fast heartbeat, hunger, confusion, irritability and blurred vision. Treat with 15 g of fast-acting sugar and recheck in 15 minutes.…
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Question
# Signs of low blood sugar (hypoglycemia)

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
Shakiness, sweating, fast heartbeat, hunger, confusion, irritability and blurred vision. Treat with 15 g of fast-acting sugar and recheck in 15 minutes. Severe lows need [glucagon](https://www.glpatlas.com/drugs/glucagon/) and emergency help.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.

URL: https://www.glpatlas.com/questions/how-to-use-insulin-pen/
Title: How to use an insulin pen
Summary: Attach a new needle, prime with 2 units, dial the dose, inject at 90 degrees into the stomach or thigh, hold for about 10 seconds, then remove and discard…
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Question
# How to use an insulin pen

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
Attach a new needle, prime with 2 units, dial the dose, inject at 90 degrees into the stomach or thigh, hold for about 10 seconds, then remove and discard the needle. Rotate sites. Never share pens.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.

Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Question
# Does insurance cover Wegovy, Zepbound or Ozempic?

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
Coverage depends on the plan and the diagnosis. Diabetes uses (Ozempic, Mounjaro) are widely covered; weight-management coverage varies and often needs prior authorization. Medicare arrangements announced in 2025 changed access for some beneficiaries; check your plan's formulary.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.

Title: Who qualifies for Wegovy or Zepbound?
Summary: Adults with a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 or more with at least one weight-related condition (such as high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes or high…
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Question
# Who qualifies for Wegovy or Zepbound?

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
Adults with a BMI of 30 or more, or 27 or more with at least one weight-related condition (such as high blood pressure, type 2 diabetes or high cholesterol), under US labels. A prescriber also checks contraindications such as a family history of medullary thyroid cancer.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.

Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Question
# How to choose a GLP-1 telehealth provider

✓Last reviewed October 20, 2026 · Written by [Dr. George Grunberger](https://www.glpatlas.com/about/#editor) · Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress · [How we review](https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/)

Short answer
Choose services whose prescribers are licensed in your state, that do a real medical assessment, dispense FDA-approved products through licensed pharmacies, and are LegitScript-certified. Avoid services selling 'research' or unbranded vials without clear sourcing.
General information based on official labels. Your prescriber or pharmacist can advise on your situation.

URL: https://www.glpatlas.com/glossary/
Title: GLP-1 and Diabetes Glossary
Summary: Plain-English definitions of GLP-1 and diabetes terms: GLP-1, GIP, A1C, basal insulin, titration, half-life, boxed warning, compounded drugs and more.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

Reference
# GLP-1 and diabetes glossary

14 plain-English definitions of the terms you will meet on labels, in trials and at the pharmacy.

 div" placeholder="Filter terms…" aria-label="Filter glossary terms">

**A1C**: A blood test showing average blood sugar over about 3 months.

**Basal insulin**: Long-acting insulin that covers background needs between meals and overnight.

**BMI**: Body mass index — weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared.

**Boxed warning**: The FDA's strongest label warning.

**Compounded drug**: A drug mixed by a pharmacy for a patient; not FDA-approved.

**GIP**: Glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide — a gut hormone targeted by tirzepatide.

**GLP-1**: Glucagon-like peptide-1 — a gut hormone that raises insulin, lowers appetite and slows digestion.

**Half-life**: Time for the amount of a drug in the body to fall by half.

**Hypoglycemia**: Low blood sugar.

**MASH**: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis — a form of fatty liver disease.

**MTC**: Medullary thyroid carcinoma — the cancer named in GLP-1 boxed warnings.

**Off-label**: Use of a drug for a purpose not on its approved label.

**Prior authorization**: Insurer approval needed before a drug is covered.

**Titration**: Gradual dose increases to improve tolerance.
No term matches.

Title: About us
Summary: Who we are and why this site exists. GLP Atlas is an independent GLP-1, weight-loss and diabetes medicine reference for the US and Canada.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

# About us

GLP Atlas is an independent reference on GLP-1, incretin and insulin medicines for readers in the United States and Canada. We explain what each medicine is approved for, how it is dosed according to its official label, its risks, and the legal ways to obtain it.

**We do not sell, ship or broker medicines.** We never process orders and never ask readers to contact us to buy anything.

Editor: **Dr. George Grunberger**. Medical review: pending — clinician review in progress.

URL: https://www.glpatlas.com/editorial-policy/
Title: Editorial policy
Summary: How we research, review and update pages. GLP Atlas is an independent GLP-1, weight-loss and diabetes medicine reference for the US and Canada.
Last reviewed: 2026-10-20

# Editorial policy

- Every page is written from primary sources: FDA and Health Canada labels, manufacturer releases and peer-reviewed trials.

- Each drug page is reviewed by a licensed clinician before publication and on every major update. The reviewer's name and date appear on the page.

- Pages carry a "last reviewed" date and are re-checked when labels or prices change.

- Commercial partners never see or approve content before publication.
- Corrections: email editor@glpatlas.com; we respond within 5 business days.

# Affiliate disclosure

GLP Atlas may earn a commission when readers use links to licensed telehealth services or pharmacies. We only link to providers that require a prescription and are verified (for example, LegitScript-certified or listed on safe.pharmacy). Commissions never affect our medical content.
